analysis.title: The Strong Outlook for Liquid Alternatives: Why GMO Is Allocating Multi-Asset Portfolios to Liquid Alts Today
key_insights: GMO describes its outlook for liquid alternative strategies as unusually strong and gives six reasons: positive cash rates, wide valuation spreads, industry evolution, competitive fees, better appeal than other investments, and elevated risk of an AI trade unwind.
Liquid alts seek returns over cash, so higher cash rates raise total returns.

Valuation spreads are wider than normal across assets, for example U.S. vs. European stocks and semiconductors vs. industrials. Most liquid alts take long-short relative value positions, so this widens their opportunity set.

Mutual funds can now replicate hedge fund results within set risk parameters. Banks offer services that mimic prime brokers, listed derivatives and exchange-traded strategies have expanded the range of long and short positions, and basket swaps allow customized short selection.
Hedge fund strategies historically charged a 2% management fee plus a 20% performance fee, often with no hurdle. GMO says strategies with competitive fee structures are now available.
GMO prefers liquid alts to credit, where spreads are still historically tight, and to expensive stocks.
ALTA is not designed as a tail-risk hedge but is managed for low correlation to equities. GMO expects it to perform well in an AI unwind.

ALTA's largest risk allocations are long-short strategies that short the frothiest parts of the AI ecosystem, quality long-short positions that tend to be defensive in equity drawdowns, and a global macro exposure that is net short equities today.
Global Asset Allocation Strategy (65/35 stock/bond benchmark) holds 17% in ALTA. Benchmark-Free Allocation Strategy holds 30% in alts, 13% of it in ALTA, plus Equity Dislocation and Emerging FX.
GMO's conclusion is that investors need more than stocks and bonds, because bonds do not protect in all environments.

trade_ideas.description: Allocate multi-asset portfolios to liquid alternatives (GMO Alternative Allocation Strategy, ALTA) in place of credit or expensive equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Positive cash rates, wide valuation spreads, and positioning that should perform well in an AI unwind.
trade_ideas.risk: Management and operational risk, leverage risk, and derivatives and short sales risk, per the report's risk disclosure.

trade_ideas.description: Benchmark-Free Allocation Strategy: Equity Dislocation (value vs. growth stocks) and Emerging FX (cheap EM currencies) as opportunistic ideas
trade_ideas.rationale: GMO calls these its two favorite opportunistic ideas today, exploiting the value-growth dislocation and the cheapness of EM currencies.

risk_factors: Elevated risk of an unwind in the AI trade
Leveraging risk from derivatives and securities lending
vol_and_positioning: GMO's Alternative Allocation Strategy is managed for low correlation to equities and is positioned to benefit from an AI trade unwind. It is not a tail-risk hedge.
Equity valuation spreads between regions and between value and the market are at 76th to 97th percentile levels as of 9/30/2026, per GMO's Exhibit 1.
ALTA's global macro exposure is net short equities. Its long-short strategies short the frothiest parts of the AI ecosystem.
